Key Activities: Participates as a member of project teams in the conduct of evaluation studies related to programs, policies and initiatives, to evaluate their relevance and performance, under the supervision of the Evaluation Manager.

Undertakes assigned tasks related to specific elements of evaluation projects such as, conducting literature and data research, identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data; participating in the conduct of interviews, and focus groups, applying analytical tools and techniques to determine implications of evaluation results and formulating conclusions.

Provides support in the assessment of current and future requirements for data; gathers and acquires information and analyzes databases; and participates in the conduct of socio-economic analyses and cost-benefit analysis of programs, under supervision.

Provides input on the interpretation of data to support findings and conclusions concerning various elements of evaluations. Recommends to the Evaluation Manager, enhancements to methods for retrieving data as well as information used in the conduct of socio-economic analyses and cost-benefit analyses.
Provides the Evaluation Manager with supporting data for sections of reports, presentations, briefing notes and memoranda for senior management on elements of program evaluations of various programs.
Attends departmental and inter-departmental meetings, when required, to discuss files / issues and evaluation requirements.

Communication: Speaking skills are required to discuss data requirements with Statistics Canada clients and evaluation colleagues; and to communicate with colleagues and outside professionals to obtain data related to Statistics Canada and external evaluation studies.

Speaking and writing skills are required to establish and maintain positive relations with Statistics Canada clients and stakeholders within and outside the Agency. The incumbent is required to communicate with clients in the data acquisition process; prepare statistical and narrative summaries for review by the  Evaluation Manager, provide progress reports, and brief the Evaluation Manager on the activities and processes being followed.
Verbal skills are required to participate in interviews, focus groups and discussions with Statistics Canada clients on data requirements and to obtain appropriate information to be used in studies.
Knowledge of Specialized Fields: Knowledge of theories and principles of economics, socio-economic, demography and statistics to: participate in the conduct of Statistics Canada evaluation studies as a member of project teams, and to interpret and analyze statistical information and databases related to various elements of Statistics Canada evaluations.

Knowledge of theories, methods and techniques of research, including social science research and analysis in order to: undertake literature and data research in support of Statistics Canada evaluation studies; identify, synthesize and analyze qualitative and quantitative research data; conduct interviews and participate in focus groups.

Knowledge of program evaluation and performance measurement theories, processes and practices for participating in the conduct of evaluation studies, making recommendations concerning the nature and scope of studies and study approaches, as well as providing supporting data for sections of reports, memoranda and briefing notes based on elements of studies conducted.
Contextual Knowledge: Knowledge is required of the mission, mandate, organization, and objectives of Statistics Canada accountabilities and policies. This knowledge is required to carry out data research, collection and compilation assignments under the supervision of the Evaluation Manager.

Basic knowledge is required of mandate and evaluation policies of the central agencies related to program evaluation, Statistics Canada, and government priorities for Statistics Canada, to carry out data research and compilation assignments related to Statistics Canada program evaluation, under supervision.
Research and Analysis: Undertakes literature and data research in support of Statistics Canada evaluation studies, under the supervision of the Evaluation Manager. The position identifies and recommends to the Evaluation Manager the usefulness and accessible sources of data to be used in studies.

Collects diverse data and information from a variety of sources, including interviews, departmental documents and those of other government departments, as well as information from provincial and territorial governments and the Internet. The position also applies established methods and techniques used for sorting, summarizing, analyzing and interpreting data.
Conducts analyses and interpretation of data collected during evaluation studies under the supervision of the Evaluation Manager, as a junior member of project teams.
The objectives and purpose of the evaluation studies are defined by the Evaluation Manager, who also determine the extent, scope and terms of reference for the studies.

Key Activities: Prepares, edits, validates and disseminates statistical metadata, ensuring that it is correctly loaded to the corporate metadata repository.
Under guidance, provides assistance and advice to internal clients with respect to statistical metadata, documented standards and relevant policies, directives and guidelines.

Provides feedback on current or proposed methods and procedures for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata; and participates in the testing of new procedures and systems.
Provides input to documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals related to the production and dissemination of statistical metadata and assists with the delivery of training.
Under guidance, assists with statistical metadata quality evaluations and provides input to reports for clients and management.
Participates on teams tasked with the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.

3. Communication: Liaises with other statistical metadata specialists, subject matter specialists, survey managers and management in order to develop and translate requirements into specifications for the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata; to negotiate procedural modifications, priorities and target dates; and to suggest improvements to methods, procedures and systems.

Contributes written information to be used as input to documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals which explain and clarify the policy requirements, methods, procedures and systems used to produce, store, disseminate and evaluate statistical metadata and assists with the delivery of training.

Contributes written information to be used as input to reports which describe the results of metadata quality evaluations and which are used by clients and management in the enhancement of statistical metadata management programs.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of statistical metadata concepts and frameworks used within Statistics Canada, the Government of Canada and internationally and knowledge of how those concepts and frameworks are used and reflected in policies, methods and procedures relating to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata in order to prepare, edit and validate statistical metadata and to provide advice and assistance to clients.

Knowledge of methods, procedures and systems used for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata and the potential impacts of new or modified methods, procedures and systems on workloads and clients in order to provide advice and assistance to clients; to participate in testing and to provide feedback on current and proposed methods for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating metadata; to provide input to procedures and training manuals; and to provide input to data quality reports.

Knowledge of survey and statistical program subject matter concepts and methodologies relevant to the collection, processing, certification and dissemination of data in order to assess client requirements for metadata production, storage and dissemination and to understand the requirements for, and instructions relating to, metadata quality evaluations.
Knowledge of software used in the production, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of policies, directives and guidelines directly and specifically related to the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata in order to prepare, edit and validate statistical metadata; to provide assistance, advice and training to clients; and to assist in reporting on metadata quality.

Knowledge of contacts within key client Divisions in order to establish a liaison and provide assistance and advice with respect to the production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation of statistical metadata.

Knowledge of surveys and statistical programs within Statistics Canada in order to understand program statistical metadata requirements and ensure consistency in the methods of processing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of metadata across programs.
Knowledge of program context, program sponsors, participants and clients in order to participate in the production, storage, dissemination and evaluation of statistical metadata.

Knowledge of the divisional mandate, activities, priorities and practices in order to adhere to the various statistical and administrative practices and procedures involved in the production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation of statistical metadata and to provide feedback on current and proposed methods for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating statistical metadata.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and of Statistics Canada policies, directives and guidelines in order to ensure understanding and application of the Act and these policies, directives and guidelines in the production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation of statistical metadata.
The position must have an awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of statistical information to ensure that actions are in compliance.
6. Research and analysis: Compiles information from diverse sources in order to prepare, edit, validate and evaluate statistical metadata.

Interprets client requirements in order to determine options for producing, storing, disseminating and evaluating the quality of statistical metadata and in order to determine the possible impacts of proposed modifications in methods and procedures.
Analyzes current production, storage, dissemination and quality evaluation methods, procedures and systems in order to propose enhancements or alternatives.

Analyzes changes in methods, procedures and systems used to produce, store, disseminate and evaluate the quality of statistical metadata in order to determine the need to update statistical metadata or adapt it to new formats and to determine where updates are required to existing documentation, procedures manuals and training manuals.
Evaluates selected indicators of statistical metadata quality across survey and statistical programs in accordance with pre-defined quality guidelines.

Key Activities: Supports the conduct of studies and/or projects using established quantitative statistical data analysis methods and software such as Python, SAS, STATA, R, E-Views, SPSS or other similar software.
Conducts data preparation techniques, for example in data extraction, data cleansing, data transformation, data validation, ascertaining data quality, conformity to standards, or data origin.
Organizes and consolidates information relevant to the defined objectives of studies. Maintains work files.
Attends Departmental meetings, and interdepartmental and stakeholder meetings (as required), to gather data/information.
Participates in project teams and working groups to support data management, research and analysis, and other unit activities.

Communication skills: Communication skills are required to maintain networks across the branch and the federal community of practice to share best practices in advanced analytics.
Provides advice, information and guidance to data users and clients regarding governance concepts used to protect and optimize the utility of Statistics Canada’s data assets.

Writing skills are necessary to draft clear and simple analytical reports, briefings and presentation material using data visualization tools for managers and clients with varying levels of knowledge and understanding of data science. Information must be impartial and clearly presented to minimize the potential for misinterpretation.

As assigned, discusses data requirements with operations managers responsible for data collection, other subject matter and systems specialists, clients or service providers to comprehend and elaborate the conditions within which statistical development and operations will occur.

There is a requirement to liaise with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject matter requirements into specifications for data development, and to suggest improvements to ongoing programs.
Knowledge: The work requires knowledge of data science and its life cycle, including data capture and acquisition, data extraction, warehousing, cleansing, processing, mining, clustering, modeling, summarization, reporting, visualization, business intelligence, and exploratory/ confirmatory, predictive analysis, regression, text mining, and qualitative analysis. This knowledge is required to optimize the use of the Statistics Canada’s data assets and to provide leading edge thinking and methodologies to data analytics.

The work requires knowledge of the theories, principles, practices, and methodologies of statistics and mathematics in order to conduct the requisite modelling that provides meaningful information for policy and program decisions by management.

Knowledge of techniques and methods of information collection and analysis, evolving information sources, survey methodologies, data risk assessment, impact and quantitative analysis in order to assess the quality of data and identify and mitigate risks to its integrity.

Data literacy skills are needed to derive meaningful information from data, including the knowledge needed to read, analyze, interpret, visualize and communicate data, as well as understand the use of data in decision-making. Data literacy includes data stewardship and the ability to assess the quality of data, protect and secure data, and safeguard their responsible use. This is needed to develop briefings, presentations and dashboards that contain valid and reliable data.

Basic knowledge of theories, principles and techniques of research is required including; hypothesis formulation and validation; model design and interpretation, experimental and comparative study designs; surveys, simulations, file reviews and case studies; qualitative and quantitative analysis including statistical sampling and cost benefit analysis; computer assisted analysis packages; and the strengths and weaknesses of these methods, tools and techniques in order to recommend and select project methodologies.

The work requires a basic knowledge of the mandate, vision, values, culture, organization, legislation, programs, business lines and operations of Statistics Canada. This is needed to ensure the alignment of the data analytics strategy with the department’s business intelligence requirements.

The work requires knowledge and understanding of the governance structures of Statistics Canada’s partnerships in order to assess data provided by other levels of government for validity and integrity.

Basic knowledge of Departmental, Central Agencies and Library and Archives Canada policies pertaining to the handling, tracking, filing and storing of sensitive and confidential material and information holdings, including electronic records.

Key Activities: Participates in the implementation, conduct and maintenance of manual and automated operations for the collection, coding and processing of data.
Evaluates collection and coding methods, procedures and results and recommends alternatives.
Provides assistance and advice to users on methods and practices of collection and coding.
Participates on data collection and operations teams.
Provides input to training materials concerning data collection operations and assists in training delivery.

technical activities, skills, responsibi: Responds orally and in writing to enquiries from managers, employees and the general public to provide information on the operation of divisional systems and processes and the use of program results.
Writes survey information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports.
Designs and prepares statistical tables, charts, graphs and explanatory text for use in regular and ad-hoc publications.
Prepares reports and recommendations outlining options and requirements for the operation of statistical collection and processing systems.

Meets with subject matter and systems specialists, clients, service providers and others, in order to comprehend and elaborate on the conditions within which statistical operations will occur. There is a requirement to understand the issues and resolve differences that can affect the efficiency of the division's operations and quality of outputs.

Contacts data suppliers or respondents to obtain their collaboration in responding to surveys, to clarify problems or irregularities. This may necessitate having to explain technical procedures for obtaining the data in the appropriate format, or to clarify and explain statistical concepts.
Participates in departmental meetings and working groups in order to share knowledge within an area of operational expertise.
4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of the underlying statistical and economic principles and concepts required for the collection, coding and processing of data.
Knowledge of the concepts, methods and techniques used in the management and control of statistical collection, coding and processing activities.
Knowledge of methods, techniques and practices used to verify statistical data and to ensure reliability and consistency to specifications.

Knowledge of methods and practices of operating personal computers in a network environment and of using databases and software packages (word processing, statistical analysis, graphics, spreadsheets, etc.) to prepare correspondence, reports and presentations.
5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of systems analysis and design, computer processing and data flows, general software packages and computer languages, for designing the specifications for testing of applications, the application and conversion of databases, and the maintenance and use of databases both for regular production of statistical data and for ad hoc manipulations and retrievals.

Knowledge of developments and changes in the subject area that may affect the efficiency and validity of data collection, coding and processing in order to devise and modify operational systems and processes.

Knowledge of divisional mandates, objectives, programs, policies and activities to adhere to the various statistical and administrative practices and procedures involved in the collection, coding and processing of statistical data.

Knowledge of data sources and contacts within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability; and external to Statistics Canada to obtain collaboration in the provision of statistical information and to verify the accuracy of data.

Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies  to ensure understanding and application in the collection, coding and processing of data. The position must have a particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance.
6. Research and analysis: Analyses changes to data sources and outputs, to determine their impact on the integrity and completeness of program results.
Assesses and reviews system requirements for use by computer analysts and programmers in reviewing existing systems or in developing new processing systems.

Analyses reported data and work results and prepares reports for program managers or subject matter specialists, presenting findings on how the survey was conducted, problems encountered in implementing concepts, definitions, classifications and other instructions, and recommending alternatives.

Identifies statistical trends and developments.

Under guidance, participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.

Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.
